transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. OE on your LG means: Cannot drain - no drain for ~13 min (kinked/clogged drain hose or clogged drain pump filter). From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked pump filter / foreign object in the pump path. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (also called the drain filter or trap), and it's a free fix. On most washing machines it's behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front. Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?
I already said I'm not unscrewing that filter, it flooded my kitchen last time and I've got a laminate floor. Is there anything else I can check that doesn't involve the filter?

Yes, you can check if the drain hose is kinked or blocked. You should also ensure the machine is not overloaded with too many clothes. A noise like that while it tries to empty, together with the water not going, usually means something is caught in the pump filter or in the pump just behind it, so the pump filter is the first thing to check, and it's often a free fix. On most washing machines it's behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front. Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?
Ok, I checked the hose. The machine was pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it, so I've pulled it out and straightened it. Do I just run it again now?

No, do not run the machine yet as it is still full of water. You need to drain the remaining water and check if the filter or pump is blocked before attempting another cycle. Next, run a drain or spin-only programme and listen near the bottom front of the machine while it tries to pump out. Does the water pump away, and can you hear the pump humming or is it silent?
I ran the spin again after straightening the hose. It drained a little slower than normal, then OE came up again. The pump hums and there's an occasional rattle. Water's still in the drum.

With the filter out, shine a torch into the filter opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with a finger. Does it turn freely, was anything caught in it, is it jammed, or do the vanes look broken?
I'm not taking the filter out, I've told you that already. Could my husband do it at the weekend instead? Is there anything I can safely do before then without unscrewing it?

Yes, your husband can wait until the weekend to handle the repair. You cannot safely clear a blockage or fix the pump issue without accessing and removing the filter at the bottom of the machine. Next: If the machine still holds water, follow the appliance's safe residual-water draining procedure/manual FIRST - opening the pump filter with water inside can release a large amount of water. Let me know what you find.
What's the safe way to get the water out of the drum, though? I don't want another flood on my laminate. I've got towels and a baking tray, but I'm not unscrewing the filter.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. You can use a wet/dry vacuum cleaner or a sponge to remove the standing water from the drum. Do not attempt to open the filter while the machine is full, as this will cause flooding on your laminate floor. Next: Inspect and clean the accessible pump filter where the model design allows. Let me know what you find.
